endpoints.description: Our levels in the MCP registry's v0.1 format, for catalogs that read a registry (base URL /api/registry): the MCP servers the official registry lists that belong to a product we drove, each with our level under _meta["com.agentdrives/drive"]. Cursor pages as the v0.1 API; also /api/registry/v0.1/servers/{name}/versions and /versions/{version} (or latest)

endpoints.name: AgentDrives: make sure AI agents can run your product
endpoints.description: Every product in the directory (open data, CC BY 4.0): each one driven by our agent, with its agent level, part scores, drive date and origin (editorial or owner, with disclosure when the owner paid). Sorted by level, then work done, then minutes to the first call

endpoints.name: AgentDrives: make sure AI agents can run your product

endpoints.name: AgentDrives: make sure AI agents can run your product
endpoints.description: Dispute your product's published result (a verified claim on its domain, else 403 claim_not_verified). A case opens; while no dispute re-drive of the product ran in the last 30 days, a confirm re-drive of the agent's path is queued (its result shows on the listing once reviewed). The answer comes in writing

endpoints.name: AgentDrives: make sure AI agents can run your product
endpoints.description: Ask our support a question (prices, plans, levels, the method, your orders, the API and MCP). When our published pages answer it, the answer comes at once, quoted, with every source's id, text and URL (answered: true). When they don't, a case opens (answered: false, case_id; without a key also a case_token) and the answer comes in writing, in the case's status. Never promised here: a level, a refund or a date we don't control. No key needed: 20 questions an hour per address without one

endpoints.name: AgentDrives: make sure AI agents can run your product

With your API key (x-api-key), two: the first answers 202 with a confirm token (and the paid drives not run yet that the deletion cancels and refunds), the same call with {token} within 5 minutes deletes. GET /api/me/delete says beforehand what it cancels and refunds

Without a key, or with no credit left, it answers 402 with both ways: pay this call (the challenges) or top up (topup, and balance_cents with a key). endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

endpoints.description: ERC20 allowance on Ethereum, Base, Arc or BNB Chain: how much a spender may move from an owner, raw and in token units, and whether the approval is effectively unlimited. Pass ?token=&owner=&spender=&chain=

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Token info and total supply for any ERC20 on Ethereum, Base, Arc or BNB Chain: name, symbol, decimals and total supply (raw and in token units), read at a named block. A contract that is not an ERC20 is refused before any charge.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Sanctions check for a wallet address on any chain: is it on the OFAC SDN list (read from Treasury's official SDN.XML, about 1,060 digital currency addresses: Bitcoin, Tron, Ethereum, USDT, Solana and more), under which entry and programs, with the list's publication date. For EVM addresses also the live freeze status from USDC (Ethereum, Base) and USDT (Ethereum), read on chain. A screen of public lists, not legal advice.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: See a web page the way a person does: pass ?url= and get a 1280x900 screenshot (JPEG, base64) of the first screen, rendered in a real headless Chrome with JavaScript executed, plus the page title, its full visible text and its links. Bot walls and empty renders are refused before any charge. Paid in USDC on Base.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Transaction status and receipt by hash on Ethereum, Base, Arc or BNB Chain: success or revert, from, to, value, contract created, gas used, effective gas price, the fee paid, block, time and log count. endpoints.description: Wallet balance on Ethereum, Base, Arc or BNB Chain: the native coin (ETH, BNB, or USDC on Arc), the chain USDC or up to 20 ERC20 tokens you list, the nonce and whether the address is a contract, read at one block. Pass ?address=&chain=&tokens=

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: ERC20 token balance of any wallet on Ethereum, Base, Arc or BNB Chain: pass ?address=&token=&chain= and get the raw balance, the decimals, the symbol and the balance in token units, with the block it was read at. endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Every URL a website publishes, from its own sitemaps: pass ?url= and we read robots.txt for Sitemap: lines (else /sitemap.xml and /sitemap_index.xml), follow nested sitemap indexes and gzipped files, and return each URL with its lastmod, up to 5,000. Unreadable files are listed with the reason. A site with no sitemap is answered before any charge.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: What a transaction on Base costs right now, in dollars, including the L1 data fee most gas trackers leave out. Read from real receipts in the latest Base blocks: the median a plain ETH transfer, a USDC transfer and a Uniswap swap actually paid (L2 fee + L1 fee), what the same gas costs at the current base fee and median tip, and the tip spread over 20 blocks. ETH priced from the Uniswap v3 WETH/USDC pool. Paid in USDC on Base.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

Bot walls and empty renders are refused before any charge. Paid in USDC on Base.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: The text of a public PDF, page by page: pass ?url= of a whitepaper, filing, invoice or paper and get every page's text with page markers, the page count and the file size. Parsed with pdf.js; up to 15 MB and 200 pages. A file that is not a PDF, will not open, or has no text layer (scanned images) is refused before any charge.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Everything about an Arc token in one call: can you sell it (a real buy-and-sell round trip through its Uniswap v4 pool, the pool fee and the hook permission bits, as a 0-100 safety score with reasons) AND what its owner can do to holders (mint, pause, blacklist, fees, upgradeable proxy, who owns it), read from the bytecode. Cheaper than the two checks bought separately.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Base name lookup: a Basename (name.base.eth) to its address, owner and public profile records (avatar, url, X, GitHub), or an address to its primary Basename, forward-verified so a spoofed reverse record is never trusted. Read on Base from the Basenames registry. Paid in USDC on Base.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: What did this transaction do? Pass ?chain=base|arc&tx=0x... and get one plain sentence plus the parts: who called which function (named from a table of common ones), every token and NFT that moved and between whom, native value, success or failure, and the gas paid in ETH and dollars on Base (ETH priced from the Uniswap v3 pool on chain) or in USDC on Arc, including native USDC that only appears as a log.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: What can the people behind this contract do to holders? Pass ?chain=base|arc&address=0x... and we read its bytecode on chain (and the code behind a proxy): mint, pause, blacklist, change fees or taxes, cap wallets, switch trading off, upgrade the code. Plus proxy type, who owns it now (renounced or a live wallet or contract) and basic token data. Facts about what the code allows, not a forecast.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Is this x402 seller real? Pass ?seller= with a host (api.example.com) or a payTo address (0x...). From Coinbase's own Bazaar counts (re-read every 6 hours) we return its listings, 30-day payers and calls, and the one number that separates customers from a test harness: how many times the average payer came back. For an Arc payTo we add its settlements from our full Arc x402 index: distinct payers and the top payer's share.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Is this link safe to send a user to? Pass ?domain= (or a URL). From public records: when it was registered and by which registrar (RDAP, the registry's own record), its DNS, who issued its TLS certificate and until when, and whether the name imitates one of 40 brands phishing kits copy (coinbase, metamask, uniswap...). A record we could not read is reported as unread, never as clean. Paid in USDC on Base.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Why will Coinbase not list your x402 endpoint, and can a standard client pay it? Pass ?url= (and &method=POST for a POST route). We read its 402 as a client does, check what Coinbase's facilitator and Bazaar enforce (accepts[0] network, the $0.001 minimum, descriptions over 500 characters, a bazaar schema that must describe info, query numbers typed as strings, routeTemplate, exposed headers), and ask Coinbase's own validator. Each problem comes with its fix.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Where does your x402 endpoint come up when an agent searches Coinbase's Bazaar? Pass ?url= and optionally &query= (up to 3; left out, your own tags are searched). For each search: your rank in the top 20, the sellers above you with their price, tags and 30-day payers, the median price, and the concrete fixes (serviceName, tags, the words your description opens with). Read live from Coinbase's public search.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Which x402 sellers have buyers who come back? From Coinbase's own Bazaar counts (re-read every 6 hours): every seller host ranked by its strongest listing with returning buyers (3+ payers, at least twice as many calls as payers), with its listings, 30-day payers and calls, price range, networks and a pattern flag (repeat buyers, single visits, or one call per wallet: a test harness). $0.01.

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Can you get out of this Base token, and what does it cost? Pass a Base token address: we find its deepest pool we can simulate (Uniswap v2, v3 or v4 against WETH or ETH, hooks included; Virtuals agent tokens through their VIRTUAL pool; Aerodrome basic and Slipstream pools against WETH, VIRTUAL or USDC), then EXECUTE a buy and a full sell in one simulated Base block and return the ETH that comes back, the round-trip cost, and the revert reason if either leg fails. Plus name, supply and whether ow

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup
endpoints.description: Base token verdict from a REAL trade, not a model: pass a Base token address and we execute a buy and a full sell of it in one simulated Base block, then grade it BASED (sells back, 3% or less lost, pool $50k+), MID, COOKED (over 10% lost or pool under $5k) or RADIOACTIVE (honeypot: the buy or the sell fails, or over 30% lost), or UNTESTED when no pool can be simulated (the market is named, no grade). Simulated: Uniswap v2/v3/v4 pools against WETH or ETH, Virtuals agent tokens through their VIRT

endpoints.name: APEX Faucet — Free APEX and USDC, three times a day · No Gas, No Signup

endpoints.description: Crypto news from 8 newsrooms in one call: CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, Decrypt, The Block, Bitcoin Magazine, The Defiant, Blockworks and Bitcoin.com News, read every 5 minutes, merged, de-duplicated and newest first, each story with its source, link, time, a short excerpt and the coins it names. Headlines and links only, credited to each newsroom; a source that fails is named in the answer, never silently missing.

endpoints.description: Check ONE email address before you send to it: pass ?email=name@domain.com and get a verdict (deliverable-domain, role-account, disposable, bad-shape or no-mail-domain) from its shape, its MX records read live over DNS, 25 known disposable-mail domains and 27 role-account names like info, support and admin. endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Check whether a specific package version has known vulnerabilities, across npm and PyPI, using the Open Source Vulnerabilities database. Use it as a supply-chain check: given a package and a version, say whether installing it would bring in a known CVE, and which version fixes it.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Static code review of a source snippet: security problems, bugs and code smells, each with a severity and a message, plus an overall quality score. Use it to review code before merging, to find hardcoded secrets and unsafe patterns, or to get a second opinion on a diff. Accepts source code in any language.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Trending GitHub repositories for a daily, weekly or monthly window, with stars, primary language and description. Use it to see what developers are shipping right now, to scout new libraries, or to find examples of a technique.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Look up a CVE in the US National Vulnerability Database: description, CVSS score and severity, affected weakness (CWE) identifiers and reference links. Use it to check whether a vulnerability a scanner reported is real and how severe it is, before deciding what to patch first.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: WHOIS and RDAP lookup for a domain: is it registered or AVAILABLE for purchase, registrar, creation and expiry dates, and status codes. Use it to check whether a domain name is free before buying it, to find when one expires, or to read ownership and nameserver details.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI
endpoints.description: Resolve DNS records (A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, CNAME) for a domain against two independent resolvers (Cloudflare and Google) and report whether their answers agree. Use it for DNS lookup, MX record checks, SPF/DKIM TXT inspection, nameserver discovery, or to debug propagation and mail routing.
